# Introduction {-}

```{r downloads, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}

  cat('<div class="downloads"><strong>Prefer to read offline?</strong> <a class="dl-btn" href="stopjerkingoff.pdf">Download the PDF</a> <a class="dl-btn" href="stopjerkingoff.epub">Download the EPUB</a></div>')
```

This book will help you conquer lust. You will stop masturbating, stop watching porn, and stop making bad decisions with women because you're thinking with the wrong head. You'll stop right away, you'll stay stopped, and you won't be miserable doing it. There are no cold showers in here, no rubber bands on your wrist, and no ninety-day streak counter to babysit. Nobody is going to shame you, and nobody is going to ask you to grit your teeth.

While you read, please don't start a willpower campaign. Make no vows, start no streaks, and don't cut down. Don't fight it with willpower. Just keep reading to the last page. Chapter 1 explains why, and why this is not permission to sin.

That probably sounds backward. Everything you've been told says the opposite: try harder, pray harder, hide the phone, reset the counter. Has any of it worked? If it had, you wouldn't be holding this book.

One caution. None of this is permission to hurt anyone. If lust has you in an affair, or using a woman, or doing anything against the law, stop that today. You don't need the last page for that.

## Before you go on {-}

This book does not replace a doctor or a counselor. Most men need nothing more than these pages. A few need a person as well. If one of these is you, get that help now, and read the book alongside it.

- **You have thoughts of ending your life or of hurting yourself.** Get medical help today. See a doctor, or call your local emergency number if you are in danger.
- **You use this to numb an old pain, or it began after something was done to you as a child.** Tell a doctor or a counselor. They keep what you say private, and they have heard it before.
- **Your urges frighten you, or what you look at has moved toward children or anything against the law.** You are not beyond help. See a doctor or a counselor now. They are there to help you, and they have heard it before.

The Appendix at the back has more.

## Is this you? {-}

Now ask yourself honestly:

- Do you watch porn, or keep drifting back to it after swearing off?
- Do you masturbate to memories, to fantasies, or to whatever crosses your feed?
- Do you do it more often than you meant to, or at times you swore you wouldn't?
- Have you made promises to yourself, or to God, that you broke within days?
- Do you reach for it without thinking, in bed or in the shower, when you're bored, stressed, lonely or can't sleep?
- Do you feel flat, guilty or disgusted with yourself afterward, and then do it again anyway?
- Do you keep it secret? Would you be ashamed if the people you respect knew how often?
- Do your thoughts drift to it at work, at dinner, or while you're talking to a woman?
- Have you made a bad decision because you wanted a woman? Have you sent the message, spent the money, told the lie, or said yes when you should have said no?
- Has it cost you energy, focus, sleep, or closeness with your partner?
- Have you ever counted days, reached a streak you were proud of, and lost it in five minutes?

If you said yes to even one of these, keep reading.

You are in good company, by the way. One pastor who writes honestly about masturbation calls it "a regular practice of most single men", and plenty of married men could raise a hand too. What sets you apart from most of them is that you've decided to do something about it.

Are you reading this for a son, a husband, a brother or a friend? The best thing you can do is get him to read it. If he won't, read it yourself. Once you see how the trap works, you'll be far better at helping him out of it. You'll also be better at keeping the next boy from walking in.

## One root, three faces {-}

Lust has three faces in this book.

The first is porn.

The second is the hand: the late-night itch, the shower routine, the reel of memories that plays when you're bored or alone. Many men quit porn and find the hand is still there. It is not harmless. It is the back door. One man quit porn twice and went back twice. Both times, he said, masturbation was what led him back.

The third face doesn't need a screen or a locked door. It's what lust does to a man around real women. He sends the message he shouldn't. He stays with the wrong woman, or chases one who is using him. He spends money to impress, says yes when he means no, and can't think straight near a pretty face. The slang of the 2020s calls this simping. The thing itself is as old as Samson. It is the same lust, making his decisions for him.

So this book goes after the root. You aren't going to manage three problems. You are going to get lust itself out of the driving seat, and the porn, the hand and the bad decisions go with it.

## One condition {-}

The method works on one condition:

**DO NOT SKIP CHAPTERS.**

Think of it as a staircase. Each chapter is a step, and each step only holds your weight because the one beneath it is there. Jump ahead to the "how to stop" chapter and you'll land on nothing.

Take the steps in order and I can promise you this method is:

- **Immediate.** You don't taper off. You stop.
- **For every man.** It works as well for the man who is at it three times a day as for the man who slips twice a month.
- **Free of misery.** No weeks of climbing the walls.
- **Free of willpower.** No gritted teeth.
- **Free of gimmicks.** No apps, no supplements, no locked boxes.
- **Clean.** You won't swap it for overeating, scrolling or drinking.
- **Lasting.** You don't have to keep walking out of the same trap.

You probably don't believe a word of that. Neither did these men, once.

One man, still in the trap, wrote:

> "I hate it, but I continually feed it."

A second, after he quit, wrote:

> "I feel like coming out from a fog that has been around me all this time."

And a third:

> "It's been over 5 years since God broke me free from the chains of pornography and masturbation addiction. I will never go back."

Notice what the free men talk about. They don't describe a miserable fight that never ends. They describe chains breaking and a fog lifting. They still keep watch, as every Christian does. But keeping watch is a long way from fighting for your life every night. That is where this book is taking you.

## Warning {-}

If you're hoping to be frightened into quitting, you'll be disappointed. There are no horror stories here about your hormones, your hairline, or what a weak and disgusting creature you are. Scare tactics have never freed anyone. If fear worked, you'd have stopped years ago.

Let's be straight about the medicine, too. Doctors will tell you that masturbation doesn't damage your body, and I'm not going to argue with them. **This book isn't about your body.** It's about your mind, your drive, your word and your soul.

I do say that lust is a sin and a thief. I say the habit robs you of drive, focus and self-respect. That is conviction, and it is the testimony of men who've lived it. You are the best witness. You know how you feel ten minutes afterward.

I won't sell you superpowers either. Some corners of the internet promise that quitting will give you a deeper voice, glowing skin and women turning their heads. I promise none of it. What you get is better than a superpower. You get yourself back.

Some of what you're about to read will be hard to believe. By the last chapter you'll believe all of it, and you'll wonder how you ever swallowed the opposite.

Here's the first thing that will sound strange: **you never chose this habit.**

Yes, you choose each time. You lock the door, you pick up the phone, you start. But did you ever sit down as a boy and decide to do this every night for the next fifteen years, whether you wanted to or not? Of course you didn't. Curiosity and puberty started it. Then the habit quietly took the wheel, and for most of us porn later poured fuel on it.

You've walked into a trap. It is one of the most subtle traps there is, because the bait is your own body. No man caught in it wants his son caught in it too. That tells you everything. Every man in the trap wishes he'd never started, and yet every man in the trap carries on. Nobody forces him. So why does he do it?

Imagine a button on your desk. Press it, and tomorrow you wake up as a man who simply never picked up this habit. No urges, no memories of it, no pull. Would you press it? Every man reading this would. Now ask why a man would press a button to be rid of something he supposedly enjoys.

This book can't press it for you. But it can show you that the button is real, and that it's closer than you think.

## The only thing stopping you is fear {-}

What keeps you in the trap isn't desire. It's **FEAR**. You fear that stopping means a long, gray stretch of frustration, craving and restless nights. That fear is built on beliefs you picked up along the way:

- "A man needs a release."
- "It's healthy. Doctors say so."
- "I'll go crazy if I don't."
- "It's the only thing that helps me sleep."
- "Everyone does it, and anyone who says he doesn't is lying."

Believe those for long enough and the fear grows. You fear the nights alone, and the hard days without your little reward. Most of all, you fear you'll never be completely free. You fear that this is just how men are, and that even if you stop, you'll spend the rest of your life fighting it. If you've already tried and failed many times, as most of us have, you'll be sure of it. One man wrote that he had failed so often he sometimes wondered whether God's grace for him had run out.

It hasn't. And you are not a hopeless case. You've only been using a method that can't work.

If you feel nervous right now, as though this isn't the right time, notice something. The habit doesn't relieve that nervousness. It causes it. And when exactly were you planning to get out? Tomorrow? Once you're married? After this stressful season? That day never arrives by itself.

## The good news {-}

The greatest gain of all is losing that fear. It won't happen at once. The fear may even grow as you read. Some men put the book down halfway, because they sense that if they keep going they'll actually have to stop. Don't be one of them.

You may be desperate to stop, or you may dread the very thought. Either way: **YOU HAVE NOTHING TO LOSE.** If you reach the last page and decide you'd rather carry on, nothing stops you. There's no shock treatment. There is only good news.

Jesus told a story about a son who took his inheritance early, left home and wasted every coin of it. People call him the prodigal son. He ended up feeding pigs, and he was starving. In that pigsty he came to himself. He got up and walked home, and he found his father running down the road to meet him. That is how it feels to walk out of this trap. Before this book is finished, that will be you.

## Two ways to fail {-}

Every man can find it easy to walk away from lust, and that includes you. Your only job is to keep reading, chapter by chapter, with your mind open. Every piece that clicks makes the next one easier.

There are only two ways to fail with this method.

**The first is not following the instructions.** Some men find this book annoyingly bossy about certain things, such as not cutting down and not using substitutes. Yes, a few men have quit with those tricks. They managed it in spite of them. A man can also cross town walking backward, but nobody recommends it.

**The second is not understanding.** Don't take anything on trust. Question what you're told, including by this book. Question what you've always assumed about sex, manhood and "needs". If you think it's just a habit, ask why you can drop other habits in a week but not this one. If you think you enjoy it, ask why you can take or leave things you enjoy far more. Why do you *have* to have this? Why does a small panic rise at the words "never again"?

You're about to do what every man in the trap secretly longs to do. You're going to be free, and you have every reason to look forward to it.

## A word on faith {-}

This book is written from a Christian point of view, and you don't have to be a Christian to use it. It isn't a sermon. If you're an atheist, play along. If you hold another faith, bring it with you. Nobody here will ask you to convert. When you hear God or sin mentioned, take it as your conscience talking. The trap works the same way on every man, and so does the way out.

The book says plainly what the Bible says: lust is sin. Jesus didn't set the bar at the act. He set it at the look. In Matthew 5:28 he says, "everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart". That one sentence covers all three faces. Porn is the look, put on a screen. The bad decisions start with the look. And the hand? Ask yourself how often you've done it with a completely empty head.

Lust is not the same as desire. Noticing that a woman is beautiful is not a sin. Wanting a wife is not a sin. God made desire, and he made it strong. Lust is desire turned into taking: the look you go back for, the woman used as material. This book is against the taking. It has nothing against the desire.

The book ends with a decision that you say out loud. For a Christian it is a prayer. For any other man it is a plain statement in his own words. Nothing is sprung on you.

If you are a Christian, hear this early. The word "sin" is here to tell the truth. It is not here to beat you. The same Bible also says, in Romans 8:1, "There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus". Hold on to both. And nothing in this book saves anyone. Freedom is God's gift. All the book can do is clear away the lies that keep a man from taking it.

## Can you be trusted? {-}

There is a bigger theme under all of this, and it is self-control. **A man who can't control his lust can't be trusted.** His partner can't fully trust him. His employer can't. Worst of all, he can't trust himself, because he has broken his own word too many times.

A Benedictine monk once gave this advice to women who want to marry: "Marry a man who can fast." He meant a man who has learned to say no to himself. Proverbs says the same from the other side. A man without self-control is like a city with its walls broken down.

Picture a soldier who shows up for duty drunk. He may be on the right side. He may even be loved. He is still unfit for service, and the men beside him go without the support they were counting on. A man ruled by lust is like that. You were made for something. This book is about getting you fit for it, and it comes back to that picture near the end.

The good news is that the reverse is also true. The man who is free of this walks differently. You're about to find out.

## If you're a woman reading this {-}

The book is written to men, and it says "he" all the way through. You are welcome in it. Women write about this same struggle, and about having no one to talk to. The trap is built the same way for you, and so is the way out. Change the pronouns and read on.

## About this book {-}

It isn't long. A few evenings will get you through it. Many men find it helps to read it a second time, so that it sticks.

Near the end there is a short chapter called If You Slip. If you fall, during the book or after it, go there. It won't scold you.

Three words come up often. *Lust* means desire turned into taking, with its three faces: porn, the hand, and the bad decisions a man makes around women. *The habit* means masturbation, with or without porn. *NoFap* is an online movement of men trying to stop both, and many of the men quoted here wrote on its forum. Visit communities like that after you've finished the book, and not before.

This book was inspired by a free book called [*The Easy Peasy Way to Quit Porn*](https://easypeasymethod.org/), known as EasyPeasy. EasyPeasy was itself a rewrite of Allen Carr's *Easy Way to Stop Smoking*. I borrowed its structure and its method, and the credit for both belongs to them. But I wanted to go further. Porn is only one face of the problem. This book goes after the root: lust itself. Any mistakes in applying the method here are mine. Like EasyPeasy, this book is shared under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike license. You may copy it, share it and adapt it, as long as you give credit and keep the same license.

So I have one request, and the last chapter comes back to it. If this book helps you, pass it on. Most men have never been told there is an easy way out.

One last time: **DO NOT SKIP CHAPTERS.**

I won't wish you luck, because luck doesn't come into it. Grace does.

"If therefore the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed." (John 8:36)
